subject: organic-chemistry-1
question: Lactic acid has the condensed structure CH3—CH(OH)—COOH. Which set of functional groups is present in this molecule?

options.text: Two hydroxyl groups and one ketone group
One ether linkage and one amine group
One aldehyde group and one ester group
One hydroxyl group and one carboxyl group

explanation:
The —OH on the middle carbon sits on a carbon with no double-bonded oxygen, so it is an alcohol (hydroxyl) group; the terminal —COOH is a carboxyl group. Lactic acid is therefore a hydroxy acid with molecular formula C3H6O3, containing 1 + 2 = 3 oxygen atoms. Students often miscount the —COOH as a separate hydroxyl plus a ketone, but a carbonyl bearing an —OH is by definition a carboxyl, and a ketone requires carbons on both sides of the carbonyl.

ELI-10: Work through the condensed formula one carbon at a time. CH3 is an unfunctionalized methyl end. CH(OH) puts an —OH on a carbon holding only hydrogens and carbons, which is the definition of an alcohol. COOH puts an —OH on a carbon that already holds a double-bonded oxygen, and that combination earns its own name and its own chemistry. Tally the oxygens you passed, 1 + 2 = 3, and you have confirmed the formula C3H6O3, which also explains why lactic acid is both very water soluble and weakly acidic.
